summary: Lists requirements for security services for HTTP, such as confidentiality, integrity, user authentication, and server authentication, including proxied services. It is informational.

eli5.summary: This lists what the web needs to be safe, like keeping secrets and being sure who you are talking to.

subtitle: Requirements for securing HTTP with confidentiality, integrity, and authentication.

tldr.problem: As HTTP carries sensitive and commercial data, it needs security services including confidentiality, integrity, and authentication of both clients and servers.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC specifies a set of security requirements that HTTP enhancements must provide, including support for multiple encryption and authentication mechanisms.
tldr.outcome: These requirements guided the development of secure HTTP protocols, ensuring that web security evolved with support for flexible mechanisms and coexistence with network-layer security.

today: RFC 2084 is Informational and has not been obsoleted. Its requirements influenced the development of HTTPS, TLS with HTTP, and subsequent HTTP security mechanisms.

sections.title: Security for Web Transactions
sections.content:
As the web carries specialized services and personal data, HTTP needs security enhancements. This RFC specifies requirements for Web Transaction Security (WTS)—any security mechanism that adds confidentiality, integrity, and authentication to HTTP transactions. WTS can be built as extensions to HTTP itself or as encapsulating security protocols that wrap around HTTP.

The RFC clarifies that WTS is independent of security at lower network layers and does not certify documents outside the transfer itself, but works alongside other security mechanisms at different protocol levels.
sections.eli5: The web needs a safe way to send private information. This document says what kinds of safety features it needs, like keeping secrets and proving identity.

sections.title: Confidentiality and Integrity
sections.content:
WTS must protect both the HTTP request and response from being read by unauthorized parties. This includes the request URI, which can contain sensitive data like form inputs. The RFC emphasizes that the identity of what is being requested is itself sensitive information that needs protection.

The system must also guarantee data integrity—assurance that the HTTP transaction including both headers and body data has not been modified in transit, for both client requests and server responses.
sections.eli5: Messages need two kinds of protection: keeping them secret so only the right person can read them, and making sure nobody sneaks in to change the message along the way.

sections.title: Authentication and Non-Repudiation
sections.content:
WTS must authenticate users to servers, allowing servers to verify who is making the request. It should also authenticate services—including gatewayed services accessed through HTTP proxies—to clients, and verify server identity regardless of intermediate proxy or caching servers. To preserve user privacy, service authentication must work even when the user remains anonymous.

The system should provide non-repudiation, meaning the sender cannot later deny having sent a request or response. Authentication should happen before sensitive request data is sent across the network.
sections.eli5: Both sides need to prove who they are: the user proves they are who they say, and the website proves it is the real website you meant to visit.

sections.title: Multiple Mechanisms and Integration
sections.content:
WTS must support multiple mechanisms for authentication and encryption. Different organizations have different policies, regulatory restrictions, and specific needs. The RFC requires that WTS be independent of HTTP content or transport mechanisms, implementable over various connection schemes and underlying protocols.

The system must negotiate among available mechanisms to allow interoperability across administrative domains and enable gradual transition to new or upgraded mechanisms. This layered approach means security services are orthogonal to and independent of other HTTP features.
sections.eli5: Different places need different kinds of locks, and they need to be able to agree on which lock to use without breaking the rest of how the web works.

sections.title: Freshness and Deployment
sections.content:
WTS must ensure transmission freshness—preventing replayed or out-of-date transactions from being accepted as current. The RFC emphasizes that WTS must integrate smoothly with both current and future HTTP versions, and be easy to deploy in real systems.

The requirements are designed to be general enough to guide various implementation approaches while specific enough to ensure interoperability. These principles supported the development of HTTP security mechanisms that became widely deployed.
sections.eli5: The system needs to know if a message is old or fake, and it should be easy for real websites to use it without breaking everything.

references.text: Berners-Lee, T., Fielding, R., and H. Frystyk Nielsen, "Hypertext Transfer Protocol -- HTTP/1.0", RFC 1945, May 1996.
Bossert, G., Cooper, S., and W. Drummond, "Requirements of Secure Object Transfer Protocols", Work in Progress, March 1995.
